keyWhy.ko: 핵심은 «우리 몸속 세균은 대부분 해가 없고 많은 수가 도움이 된다(주장)» 와 «세균은 단순한 친구도 적도 아니며, 대부분은 없어서는 안 될 동반자다(결론)» 입니다. 초록색 문장이 정답이에요.
keyWhy.en: The key ideas are the claim (most bacteria in our bodies are harmless, and many are helpful) and the conclusion (most bacteria are partners we cannot live without). The green sentences are the answers.

boxes.a: Bacteria and how they live with us

boxes.qen: How do gut bacteria help us?
boxes.a: They help digest food, make vitamins, and train the immune system

boxes.qko: 항생제를 지나치게 쓰면 무슨 일이 생기나요?
boxes.qen: What happens when antibiotics are overused?
boxes.a: Bacteria become resistant, and infections get harder to treat

sumHowto.ko: 먼저 위 세 칸을 보고, 빈칸에 알맞은 단어를 고르세요.
sumHowto.en: Look at the three boxes, then choose the right word for each blank.

sum.pre: Many people think of disease when they hear the word bacteria, but most bacteria are
. Trillions of them live in our
, where they help digest food and make vitamins. Outside the body, they break down dead plants and help make foods like
. However, when antibiotics are overused, the bacteria that survive can pass on their
. Therefore, doctors advise using antibiotics only when they are truly
, because most bacteria are partners we cannot live without.

words: all the tiny living things that live together in one place, such as the gut
the few bacteria that survive can multiply and pass on their resistance
the ability to survive a medicine that should kill you
Gut bacteria help break down food we cannot digest alone
to break down food in the body
able to protect the body from disease
They break down dead plants and animals, returning nutrients to the soil.
things in food or soil that help living things grow
this accident led to penicillin, the first antibiotic
a medicine that kills harmful bacteria

qs.q: Why have some infections become much harder to treat?
qs.qko: 왜 어떤 감염은 치료하기가 훨씬 어려워졌나요?
opts: Overused antibiotics let surviving bacteria multiply and pass on resistance
People eat too much yogurt and kimchi
evs: When antibiotics are overused, the few bacteria that survive can multiply and pass on their resistance.
Antibiotics can also harm the helpful bacteria in our gut along with the harmful ones.
It is true that some bacteria cause serious illnesses, such as tuberculosis and cholera.
Gut bacteria help break down food we cannot digest alone, and some produce vitamins such as vitamin K.
why: 항생제를 지나치게 쓰면 살아남은 소수의 세균이 늘어나면서 내성을 퍼뜨려요. 그 결과 어떤 감염은 치료하기가 훨씬 어려워졌어요.
When antibiotics are overused, the few bacteria that survive can multiply and pass on their resistance. As a result, some infections are harder to treat.

qs.q: In the text, what does "Here is the twist" mean?
qs.qko: 글에서 «Here is the twist» 는 무슨 뜻인가요?
opts: A surprising turn: fighting bacteria can cause new problems
A simple rule: kill every kind of bacteria
A new kind of bacteria found in kimchi
evs: Here is the twist: our efforts to kill bacteria can create new problems.
When antibiotics are overused, the few bacteria that survive can multiply and pass on their resistance.
However, the full picture is far more surprising.
Outside the body, bacteria are just as important.
why: «twist» 는 이야기가 뜻밖의 방향으로 바뀌는 것을 말해요. 세균을 없애려는 노력이 오히려 새로운 문제를 만든다고 하고, 항생제를 너무 많이 쓰면 내성이 퍼진다고 설명해요.
A twist is a surprising change. Our efforts to kill bacteria can create new problems, because overused antibiotics spread resistance.

qs.q: Why does the writer call bacteria partners we cannot live without?
qs.qko: 글쓴이는 왜 세균을 «없어서는 안 될 동반자» 라고 부르나요?
opts: They help us digest food and make vitamins, and they return nutrients to the soil
They cause tuberculosis and cholera in most people
They disappear forever after we take antibiotics
evs: Gut bacteria help break down food we cannot digest alone, and some produce vitamins such as vitamin K.
They break down dead plants and animals, returning nutrients to the soil.
It is true that some bacteria cause serious illnesses, such as tuberculosis and cholera.
As a result, some infections have become much harder to treat.
why: 몸속 세균은 소화를 돕고 비타민을 만들며, 몸 밖의 세균은 죽은 동식물을 분해해 흙에 영양분을 돌려줘요. 두 단서를 합치면 왜 없어서는 안 될 동반자인지 알 수 있어요.
Gut bacteria help us digest food and make vitamins, and outside the body bacteria return nutrients to the soil. Together, these clues explain why we need them.

ends: How did one moldy dish lead to the first antibiotic?
곰팡이 핀 접시 하나가 어떻게 첫 항생제가 되었을까?
What happens inside kimchi as it ferments?
김치가 익는 동안 그 속에서는 무슨 일이 일어날까?
